howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.step1: The MCP server connects to the Figma file via API and exposes its structure — nodes, styles, variables — as tools any compatible agent can call.
howItWorks.step2: When an AI agent (Cursor, Claude) needs design context, it calls those tools instead of asking for a screenshot.
howItWorks.step3: The agent receives structured data — tokens, layers, spacing — and uses it to generate code that respects the design system from the first prompt.

bio.1: I build product interfaces in React, React Native and Next.js, and connect them with the AI tooling that is transforming development.
bio.2: At Gyoza I led the implementation of Wetour (a Next.js community with an SEO focus) and Turbowash (a React Native app controlling laundry machines: payments, loyalty, and remote activation), alongside contributing to Goiko.
bio.3: My work is grounded in scalable UI architecture and in state and async data management with Zustand and TanStack Query.
bio.4: In little over a year I went from pure frontend engineering to shipping design-context-bridge: my own MCP server in production, compatible with Cursor, Claude Code, and Windsurf, giving AI agents real design context from Figma.
bio.5: When a tool I need doesn't exist, I build it.
